source.title: Structural Theory of Degrees of Unsolvability: Advances and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let R denote the semilattice of computably enumerable Turing degrees, and for each integer n > 1 let D_n denote the semilattice of Turing degrees containing sets from the nth finite level of the Ershov hierarchy. Which finite posets can be embedded into R and into D_n while preserving the appropriate order relations, and in particular, is there an effective description of the finite lattices that are embeddable in these structures while preserving lattice operations?
accepted.context_brief: Embeddable finite lattices in R and D_n

evidence.quote: (a) The problem of describing embeddable finite posets in degree structures R and Dn, n > 1 (preserving appropriate relations). A basic challenge is finding an "effective" description of finite lattices embeddable in these structures while preserving lattice operations.

accepted.question_text: Fix n ≥ 1 and finite posets P, Q_0, ..., Q_m such that each Q_i extends P. Is there an algorithm that, given these finite posets, determines whether every embedding f: P → D_n can be extended to an embedding g: Q_i → D_n for some index i ≤ m, where the successful index i is allowed to depend on the chosen embedding of P into D_n?

evidence.quote: (b) The recognition problem for the possibility of embedding extensions. We clarify whether there exists an algorithm which, given finite posets P → Q0,...,Qn, n ≥ 0, allows us to determine whether any embedding f : P → Dn can be extended to an embedding g : Qi → Dn for some i ≤ n. (Clearly, here i depends on the choice of an embedding of P in Dn.)

accepted.question_text: Does every finite lattice admit an embedding into the semilattice D_2 of d.r.e. degrees that preserves the least and greatest elements 0 and 1?

evidence.quote: There is a still unconfirmed conjecture of Downey [8] which maintains that every finite lattice is embeddable in the semilattice D2 of degrees preserving 0 and 1.

accepted.question_text: For some n > 1, or even for every n > 1, do there exist computably enumerable degrees a_0 and a_1 that form a two-sided strong minimal pair inside the n-c.e. degrees, meaning that whenever x is a nonzero n-c.e. degree with x < a_i, one has x ∪ a_{1-i} = 0'? Equivalently, in the preceding theorem, can the degree a_1 be chosen to be computably enumerable rather than merely d-c.e.?
accepted.context_brief: Two-sided strong minimal pairs of c.e. degrees

evidence.quote: Question. Do there exist c.e. degrees that form a two-sided strong minimal pair in n-c.e. degrees for each (some) n > 1? In other words, is it possible that in the previous theorem, the d-c.e. degree a1 is made into a c.e. degree?

accepted.question_text: Let P be a finite lattice and let Q be a one-point extension of P. Suppose that every embedding of P into D_2 extends to an embedding of Q. Must it then follow that every embedding of P into R also extends to an embedding of Q?
accepted.context_brief: Transfer of one-point extension property from D_2 to R

evidence.quote: Conjecture. Let P be a finite lattice and Q be its one-point extension. If every embedding of P in D2 can be extended to an embedding of Q, then this is also true for embeddings of P in R.
